title: Rapid quenching by ram-pressure stripping in a young cluster at $z = 1.7$

affiliations.text: Department of Astronomy, Example University, Madison, WI, USA
Institute for Cosmic Discovery, Cambridge, UK

abstract.content: Galaxies falling into dense cluster environments can lose their star-forming gas within a few hundred million years. Here we demonstrate the SUNA example project: a small, fully reproducible manuscript whose figures are generated by the scripts stored beside them, whose references live in BibTeX, and whose formatting compliance is checked against the journal's published author guidelines.

caption.title: H\alpha emission and the star-forming main sequence.
caption.body: **a**, Continuum-normalized spectrum around H$\alpha$ (steps) with the best-fit Gaussian model (solid). **b**, Star-formation rate against stellar mass for cluster members; the dashed line marks the quenching threshold.

caption.title: Line-of-sight velocity field of the stripped disk.
caption.body: Moment-1 map from the demo data cube; the diverging color scale is centred on the systemic velocity.

caption.title: Observed and derived properties of the stripped galaxy.
caption.body: Fitted quantities are read from results/spectrum_fit.json; the stripping radius is computed by code/stripping_model.py.

footnotes.text: Gaussian centroid of the H\alpha line from analysis/fit_spectrum.py.

availability.data: The demo data underlying this example are included in the project's data/ directory.
availability.code: Figure-generating scripts live beside their figures under figures/*/source/; the analysis pipeline is in analysis/, reusable model code in code/, and derived products in results/. Everything runs with suna_mpl via uv.
